title: Steering frontier agents without flattening them
audience: applied AI alignment researchers at a technical symposium
core_points: Framing: alignment stacks too often optimize for legibility at the cost of capability
Measurement regime we use: capability ceiling (unsteered) and steering delta (behavior with constraints)
Taxonomy of steering: rule-based, reward-based, representation-engineering, activation-steering
Empirically: hard rules lose >40% capability ceiling; soft rewards lose ~11%
Our contribution: residual-stream probes + targeted activation edits preserve 95%+ ceiling
Case study: multi-step research agent, 37% delta on open-ended tasks post-steering
Negative result: same method degrades 8% on adversarial prompt benchmark; we explain why
Connection to governance: measurement must report both axes, not just refusal rate
Open problem: there is still no clean evaluation for value-preservation under steering
Practical recipe for practitioners building production agents: a 4-step checklist
Call to the room: publish steering deltas alongside refusal rates
